title: Seven Doors of a Leaf
logline: In a bark-peeling shed, quality is judged by smell, touch and sound as much as by sight, and a grade is settled before anyone speaks.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) could enter only if a real moment allows, for example a peeling knife or the day's first quill genuinely given. Never staged.

thread_in.thread: The turn: having slowed down in the fog, the series looks at a single moment up close, in a shed where cinnamon quills are judged by smell, touch and sound before a word is spoken.

thread_out.thread: Along the southern coast from the cinnamon belt to the dry-zone salt pans: from senses working together to a heap that looks unchanged though no crystal in it is the same twice.

requirements: An active cinnamon-peeling shed willing to allow filming during real production
Workers willing to describe, in their own words, how they judge quality
Consent covering the economics of a labour-intensive trade

suggestions.name: Southern coastal cinnamon-growing belt
suggestions.why: Sri Lanka's traditional heartland for cinnamon cultivation and peeling.
suggestions.access_notes: Peeling sheds are often small family operations; access would need direct relationships.
suggestions.verify: A specific shed and willing workers are unconfirmed.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Each sense brings in only its own kind of thing: the eye brings colour, the nose brings smell, the fingers bring hardness and warmth. A peeler's quick sense that a quill is good is put together from several separate channels, each resting on a part of the living body.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ඇසට එන්නේ පැහැය, නාසයට එන්නේ සුවඳ, අතට එන්නේ තද බව හා උණුසුම පමණයි; හොඳ කුරුඳු පොල්ලක් හඳුනාගන්නේ මේ වෙන් වෙන් දොරටු කිහිපයකින් ආ දේ එකතු වීමෙනි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma teaches six 'doors' (dvāra) through which objects enter: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body and mind, and each door takes only its own kind of object, so sight takes colour, hearing sound, smell scent, taste flavour, and touch the hard and the hot or cool (C035, C036). The texts describe each of the five sense doors as a fine sensitivity inside the organ, not the visible organ itself, and the same sensitivity is also the physical 'base' (vatthu) on which that kind of sense-consciousness arises (C035, C037). What reaches the nose or tongue arrives as a blend, and it is known as this or that because it has been met before (C036).
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film follows one quill from raw bark to graded bundle and lets the viewer count the senses at work: a quill lifted to the nose, rolled between the fingers, tapped and listened to, held up to the light. When a peeler struggles to say how they know a good one, the distance between the separate channels and the single quick verdict is left for the viewer to notice.

key_terms.en: door: where an object enters and the mind goes out to it
sensitive matter: the fine sensitivity inside a sense organ
physical base on which a mind arises

lesson.caution: This is not anatomy, since the texts' sensitivity is not the retina or nerve endings, and it is not a 'guard your senses' slogan: it describes how experience comes in, not what anyone should do about it.
lesson.builds_on: After a stage about how people lose their way in doubt, restlessness and confusion, the series takes the turn it was handed, slowing down to ask where a single moment of experience comes in at all.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
